Over 50,000 Sign Petition Urging Legal Action Against Cyber Wrecking: Fans Rally to Support Kim Soo-hyun and Demand Reform

A national petition to prevent the spread of false information and protect human rights on online platforms has officially surpassed 50,000 signatures, meeting the threshold for legislative review by the Korean National Assembly.

Filed on May 22 via the National Assembly Electronic Petition site, the petition—titled “Petition to Improve the System to Prevent Repeated Spread of False Information and Human Rights Violations on Online Platforms”—calls for legal and institutional reforms against so-called "cyber-wrecking" channels such as Garosero Research Institute (Gaseyeon).

“Serious social damage is occurring due to repeated false broadcasts and human rights violations. We demand practical measures such as legal punishment and platform sanctions.”

A major example cited in the petition is actor Kim Soo-hyun, who has been unfairly targeted by fabricated claims and invasive reports. In particular, Gaseyeon made unsubstantiated allegations about the actor’s private life, including false claims of a long-term relationship with the late Kim Sae-ron—an accusation that has sparked public outrage and legal action.

Despite the baseless attacks, Kim Soo-hyun has maintained grace under pressure, with his fans and legal team firmly standing behind him. He is widely known not only for his stellar acting career but also for his reputation as a kind, respectful, and professional artist—qualities that have earned him the loyalty of fans both in Korea and internationally.

The petition also calls for broader reform beyond this individual case, urging for new laws and support systems to prevent future harm by similar online platforms. It emphasizes the need to restore victims' honor and protect families from secondary damage, stating:

> “Kim Se-ui and channels like Gaseyeon continue to spread harm for views and profit, ignoring human rights and ethical broadcasting standards. These acts can no longer be tolerated in a just society.”

Following the success of the petition’s first milestone, it will now move to the relevant National Assembly committee for review. If passed, it could mark a historic step in regulating malicious content and protecting human dignity in the digital era.

As Kim Soo-hyun’s supporters say: “We don’t just protect a star. We protect a human being.”
